## Body

For keyed long-running operations, keep the original operation's wait and the recovery window as separate clocks. Start recovery time at the first transport failure, not before the first send. A fake-clock case should advance beyond the recovery duration inside the first send, then cut it; instant-send retry fixtures miss this.

When replacing a watcher, test rewatch-before-bind and bind/report-before-rewatch. A generation check protects an extant entry; removing terminal entries and inserting new ones can forget a row's binding or report one launch again. Distinguish a previously scheduled or admitted settlement from a current watch.

For spawn replay, a HTTP-owned lock is not a shield for launch-through-row work. Verify cancellation after the pane exists and while descriptor publication is pending, not only after a pre-bind row is visible. Preserve the independently owned mutation's serialization lifetime.

Proof posture: native source probes with recording dependencies prove state transitions, not full asynchronous HTTP behaviour. Keep their grade separate from exact-head CI and from a production bounce. The reviewer still holds its PR instance until merge.

MagicWand: a deterministic replay matrix for pending row commit, delayed first-send EOF, and binding/reporting before resend, with generation/binding mutants as controls.
